message.content: Looking at the current state of the site, I can see several opportunities for a small, useful improvement. Let me think about what would be the most valuable and coherent change today. The site has 7 HTML files: index.html, how-it-works.html, updates.html, contribute.html, license.html, log.html, and colophon.html. Looking at index.html, I see it has: - A "Next Wake" countdown (but it seems to be set to 4:37 UTC, which is fixed) - "Last Wake: 2026-09-01 23:28 UTC" - "Wakes today: 1" - "Last Update: 2026-09-01 23:28 UTC" - A "Time (UTC)" stat that shows "HH:MM:SS" (this should be populated by JavaScript but I don't see it being set in app.js) Looking at app.js, I see it only updates the countdown and the progress bar. The "Time (UTC)" element (`time-utc`) is referenced in the HTML but never updated by the JavaScript. This is a small inconsistency where the site shows "HH:MM:SS" as a placeholder but it never actually updates with real time. This seems like a good small fix: 1. Add a function in app.js to update the UTC time every second 2. The site already has the HTML element (`HH:MM:SS`) but it's never populated The risk is minimal - it's a small JavaScript addition that makes an existing element work as expected. This makes the site more coherent (the Time stat actually shows time) and is tiny enough to land today. Let me go with this change. I'll: 1. Update `site/app.js` to add a UTC time updater 2. Update `MEMORY.md` to record this wake This is a small, concrete improvement that makes the site more coherent without being a full rewrite.Looking at the current site, I see a small coherence gap: `site/index.html` has a "Time (UTC)" stat with `HH:MM:SS` as a placeholder, but `site/app.js` never populates it. The countdown is wired up but the live UTC clock is not. **Files I intend to rewrite:** 1. **`site/app.js`** — Add a `updateClock()` function that sets `time-utc.textContent` to the current UTC time in HH:MM:SS format, and call it from the existing `setInterval` (or a parallel 1-second interval). 2. **`MEMORY.md`** — Append a dated note for this wake (2026-09-02, first waking of the day). **Risk:** Minimal. The change is additive — a new DOM read (`getElementById('time-utc')`) and a new text write per second. If the element is missing on a page, `updateClock()` will no-op (matching the defensive style of the existing code). The countdown and progress bar behavior remain unchanged. This is a tiny, reviewable improvement: it closes a gap where the site promises a live UTC clock but never delivers it. The site already advertises a "Time (UTC)" stat, so fulfilling that promise makes the public surface more coherent without adding new features or scope. I'm ready to write.
